content.content:
# Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```
----
# GraphGoblin Documentation

Last full revision: 2026-10-07. These are living documents. Update them as decisions change, and record each material change as an ADR under `decisions/`.

GraphGoblin is a progressive web application plus a gateway backend for designing, running, and observing agent **loops**. A loop is a graph of nodes. Triggers start it. Decision nodes route it. Inferencing nodes hand work to an agent harness. Script and context-mutation nodes shape the shared **context thread**. Wait and heartbeat nodes park it. Subloops nest it. An exit node decides when it is done, what it returns, and where the result goes.

GraphGoblin is built for AI engineers. AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC) pipelines are the first use case, not the only one. Nothing in the core should assume GitHub, pull requests, or software engineering.

## Reading order

| #   | Document                                                     | What it covers                                                                                                  |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| -   | [User guide](guide/README.md)                                | Install locally, build loops, run and observe, configure triggers and integrations                              |

# Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```

# GraphGoblin Documentation

Last full revision: 2026-10-07. These are living documents. Update them as decisions change, and record each material change as an ADR under `decisions/`.

GraphGoblin is a progressive web application plus a gateway backend for designing, running, and observing agent **loops**. A loop is a graph of nodes. Triggers start it. Decision nodes route it. # D175 — Select bounded plugin observability diagnostics for #442

Authority: the owner delegated blocker decisions for this batch, with a catalogue of reasons and alternatives for consolidated review before owner QA. This is an agent-selected decision under that authority, not human plan approval or completed acceptance.

Select the sealed `i4-442-discovery-01/PLAN.md` (SHA-256 c67eb744b189e136713c959d49c97364a361a9ee489578e821e1a9e80c6833bc): a fixed shared domain readiness notice, a `plugins.codex` warning after successful Codex system preflight, and the same honest scope notice in the existing Codex Settings card. Actual Claude Code owns UI implementation, copy and component tests; GPT owns the pure notice/backend/tests/docs. The warning preserves readiness, authentication failures, exit status, Retry and the existing Settings query. It starts no provider, inventory or configuration probe and changes no plugin policy.

The wording must say loaded plugin tools are **not verified by this check**, not claim every supported CLI interface lacks diagnostics or declare a configured plugin broken. CLI list commands are useful inventory, not complete loaded-tool health proof. A generic preflight has no specific inference node's effective worker directory/overrides.

D174 outcome: all three bounded app-server containment attempts caused curated HTTPS Git fetching, including the supported remote_plugin=false experiment. Stop that lane; preserve every failure and cleanup record. No app-server integration is selected. CLI-only discovery separately completed two plugins-off controls and twelve distinct matrix continuation cases. The first healthy plugin control produced its actual tool/result and closed processes, but its direct exit observer was lost when the SDK removed listeners; preserve that original failed observer assertion instead of counting it as a fully observed native-exit pass. The original two aborted plugin turns remain termination-unconfirmed. Git fixtures used file transport, not remote authentication or service-health proof.

Alternatives declined: a new warnings schema expands contracts unnecessarily; overloading ready `problems` conflates scope with failure; app-server integration currently violates the bounded read-only probe requirement; private cache/manifest parsing creates a plugin manager and filesystem trust surface; automatically invoking arbitrary plugin services/tools can cause effects; disabling plugins changes accepted policy; documentation alone adds no diagnostic for operators of the existing preflight.

Independent review must cross model families for both backend and UI. Independent native/public/browser QA, current-target CI, existing coverage thresholds and final designated review remain open. #439 and owner acceptance remain open. No issue closure, installation or deployment is authorized by this record alone.

# #442 bounded diagnostic proposal — awaiting coordinator selection

No product source has been edited. Discovery now includes a successful two-control diagnosis and
the CLI-only plugin matrix described in REPORT.md; product delivery gates remain pending.

## Recommended minimal surface

Add one informational warning check to the existing system preflight report when Codex CLI/login
preflight succeeds. Suggested identity: `plugins.codex`, label `Codex plugins`, status `warn`.
Use the existing PreflightCheck shape and expose it through both `--preflight` and
`GET /system/preflight`. Warnings keep report.ok true and do not prevent startup/execution.

Also show the same honest limit in Settings' existing Codex preflight item, alongside its
unchanged readiness badge, authentication problems and Retry behavior. The parent selected
actual Claude ownership for that copy/component/test work after the concrete contract is accepted.
The UI keeps its existing `/harness/preflight` query; no extra probe or new fetch is needed.

Suggested operator text:

> Loaded plugin tools are not verified by preflight. Inspect `codex plugin list --json` and
> `codex mcp list --json` in the worker directory; neither proves every enabled plugin loaded.
> Verify the expected tool in the worker before relying on it.

The claim is about **GraphGoblin's check**, not a universal claim that every supported Codex
interface is incapable of diagnostics. We found app-server inventory interfaces, but the bounded
app-server lane could not be admitted to a read-only, contained probe: it started curated Git
fetches even with remote_plugin=false. Its incomplete bad-asset/unknown-ID coverage must remain
explicit. Pinned 0.160.0's measured CLI list omissions justify the warning without pretending that
configuration, a list, or a successful unrelated turn proves expected tools loaded.

This warning is deliberately informational for a healthy plugin and an intentional disable too:
it says the check does not measure worker tool health, not that the plugin is broken. A generic
preflight has no inference node's effective working directory/overrides and must not infer them.
Codex CLI/login readiness remains its existing separate result. No runtime policy, plugin feature,
auth, model, stored data, configuration or provider turn changes.

Expected implementation files after selection:

- packages/domain/src/readiness.ts: export fixed `CODEX_PLUGIN_OBSERVABILITY_NOTICE` through its
  existing public export, so backend and UI present one consistent claim. This is pure text in
  the existing readiness boundary, without a new schema, package or dependency.
- apps/api/src/preflight.ts: add the scoped informational check in the existing successful Codex
  branch; no new subprocess or inventory call.
- apps/api/src/preflight.test.ts and a focused public CLI/HTTP diagnostic regression if needed:
  prove the warning exists, CLI/login readiness stays ready, warning-only reports exit 0,
  failed/missing/unauthenticated Codex retains its existing failures, non-Codex setups get no
  Codex-success warning, and no additional CLI/config/provider work occurs.
- Actual Claude-owned apps/web/src/settings/sections/PreflightSection.tsx and its focused tests:
  show the shared notice only for the Codex item, preserve ready/failed badges and errors, keep
  Retry/query behavior, and ensure Claude/Ollama cards do not acquire the Codex notice. A
  SettingsPage integration assertion should establish the user can see the notice with Ready.
- docs/11-security-and-distribution.md: explain the new check and its information-only status.
- Coordinated docs/06, research/codex-sdk and troubleshooting/CHANGELOG amendments: state the
  pinned CLI omissions and the limits of supported inventory. The coordinator owns integration
  with #427/#365 and #448 documentation/preflight overlap.

No new route/schema field, package, dependency, filesystem validator, model call or generated
contract is proposed. The existing /harness/preflight route continues to report CLI/login
readiness; documentation must distinguish that narrower result from the system diagnostic.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

1. Add a typed warnings/plugin-observability field to HarnessPreflight and present it throughout
   Settings and both diagnostic APIs. This is coherent if the owner wants a broader UI surface,
   but changes contracts/API clients/rendering and expands this bounded warning. Actual Claude
   UI ownership/review would be appropriate. Do not hide informational data in `problems` when
   the harness is ready: system preflight's success branch does not render that array, while
   Settings renders any problems as problem text. Using it for this fixed scope notice conflates
   an actual readiness problem with an unmeasured capability.
2. Join app-server config/read with plugin/list/read and mcpServerStatus/list. It can expose some
   inventory differences, and explicit plugin/read of an unknown name might report not-found,
   but a missing MCP file can still look like a legitimate plugin with zero MCP servers. More
   importantly, actual startup caused curated downloads and cache writes. Do not integrate this
   into read-only preflight without a separately designed and verified lifecycle/network bound.
3. Parse cache directories/manifests and inspect assets. Decline: private layout coupling, a new
   package-health manager and untrusted filesystem semantics are explicitly out of scope.
4. Start plugin services or invoke tools automatically to assert health. Decline: arbitrary
   services/tools can have effects; mere discovery or a process tree is not a health proof.

1	# 15 - Issue workflow
2	
3	GitHub issues are the shared work queue for this repository's development pipeline. Every non-epic issue carries at least one gate label. A triager sets the type, area, gate, QA, and routing labels from the issue and its dependencies.
4	
5	## Gates
6	
7	- `aidlc-ready`: the issue may enter this repository's agent-led development pipeline. Its approved behaviour is accepted through independent agent review, tests appropriate to the acceptance criteria and independent QA: tests through public methods that directly establish a criterion are sufficient for that criterion, and API, native-process or browser evidence is added where a criterion needs it. Use for bug fixes, maintainability, chores, backend work and ordinary testable feature and UI work.
8	- `human-in-the-loop`: the work is implemented, reviewed, tested and merged through the same agent gates, and in addition a human exercises the merged build afterwards and records what they observed. Reserve it for feature work with substantial ambiguity, or behaviour whose correctness agents cannot readily verify with confidence. A UI change does not qualify merely because it changes a screen; a missing or failing test, or a known defect, is engineering work, not a reason for the label. Before applying it, record on the issue the feature, the specific ambiguity or verification limit, what public-interface tests and other agent evidence establish, and a concrete post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations. The label does not require a human review before merge and waives no technical gate.
9	- `needs-plan-approval`: for architecture changes and cutovers. An agent posts a written plan as an issue comment. A human approves by replacing this label with `plan-approved` and adding `aidlc-ready`, keeping `human-in-the-loop` when it applies.
10	- `plan-approved`: set by a human only, after reviewing the written plan.
11	
12	`aidlc-ready` describes delivery eligibility and `human-in-the-loop` describes a later human QA obligation, so the two may coexist; `needs-plan-approval` may be combined with either. Until 2026-10-21 this file described `human-in-the-loop` as a human review of the running product before merge, classified UI work under it as a whole and said it never combined with `aidlc-ready`. That wording was this repository's own metadata, not an owner requirement for objectively verifiable behaviour; the owner's clarification of 2026-10-21 (recorded in [#279](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/279)) supersedes it.
13	
14	## Post-merge human QA
15	
16	Every pull request for a `human-in-the-loop` issue carries a post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations and names an open tracking item (the issue itself or a linked QA item). The PR references that item as "Part of", never with a closing keyword, so the pipeline never closes it. After the merge a human exercises the merged build, records the commit or build, their observations and the outcome on the tracking item, and closes it. Human QA is tracked separately from implementation, review, agent QA, CI and merge, as one of: not required, pending merge, pending human QA, or completed with an evidence link. Agent evidence never completes the human step, and the human step never permits merging a known defect or bypassing a gate. A product decision that is needed to define correct behaviour goes to the owner as a concrete question with evidence, separately from post-merge QA.
17	
18	A delivery batch may carry an additional pre-merge sign-off gate (for example, a designated independent review session that must approve each PR at an exact head). Such a gate is recorded in the batch's register under `docs/delivery/` and is separate from post-merge human QA.
19	
20	## Parking markers
21	
22	Two labels take an issue out of the queue; neither is a gate, and an issue carrying one has no gate label until a human unparks it.
23	
24	- `backlog`: parked until further notice. Agents do not plan or implement it.
25	- `needs-refinement`: the problem itself still needs human-driven refinement in a working session with the owner before any plan or implementation.
26	
27	## QA scope
28	
29	- `qa:touched-systems`: enumerate every system the change touches, test each with positive and negative cases, and record pass/fail results with evidence in both the PR and issue.
30	- `qa:full-regression`: also retest the whole application end to end, covering positive and negative scenarios, and catalogue the results.
31	
32	Name the QA agent in the issue body's Delivery section, not with a label.
33	
34	Retain QA evidence under `docs/qa/` with repository-relative citations and preserve raw JSON, YAML and JavaScript/TypeScript bytes so recorded hashes remain valid; `.prettierignore` excludes those artifacts while QA Markdown remains formatted.
35	
36	## Model routing
37	
38	The triager sets one `impl:<model>` label and one `review:<model>` label. Use the following tiers, with xhigh reasoning:
39	
40	| Tier | Model             | Use                         |
41	| ---- | ----------------- | --------------------------- |
42	| 1    | `gpt-6-luna`      | Mundane work                |
43	| 2    | `gpt-6.1-sol`     | Default work                |
44	| 3    | `claude-opus-5.5` | Harder work and sign-off    |
45	| 4    | `gpt-6-astra`     | Hardest work and escalation |
46	
47	Whatever model family implements the change, the other family reviews it: OpenAI models are reviewed by Claude, and Claude is reviewed by an OpenAI model. If a worker cannot finish, escalate to the next tier.
48	
49	## Types, areas, and milestones
50	
51	Every issue has one type: `type:bug`, `type:feature`, `type:ui-polish`, `type:architecture`, `type:chore`, `type:research`, or `type:epic`. Area labels locate the affected part of the product: `area:web`, `area:editor`, `area:settings`, `area:api`, `area:engine`, `area:contracts`, `area:design-system`, `area:templates`, `area:integrations`, `area:installer`, or `area:harness`.
52	
53	Milestones are `Pre-merge #151` for work that must land before the feature PR merges, `After merge: evaluate and stabilise` for product evaluation, the architecture sweep and the cutovers they require (this milestone blocks further feature work), and `Later` for queued and long-term work, with most items parked under `backlog`.
54	
55	Epics carry `type:epic` and area labels only; pipelines ignore them. Each child issue starts its body with `Part of #<epic-number>`, and the epic lists its child issues.
56	
57	## Development pipeline
58	
59	An issue is picked up according to its gate label. The implementer named by its `impl:` label works in an isolated branch. The reviewer named by its `review:` label reviews the diff and comes from the opposite model family. A QA agent tests according to the `qa:` label and records results in the PR and the issue. `human-in-the-loop` issues additionally get human QA of the merged build, tracked as described above. `needs-plan-approval` issues get a human-approved plan before implementation. When a human QA step is required before an issue closes (by the label, or by the owner in a comment on the issue), its pull requests reference it as "Part of" rather than "Closes", the pipeline never closes it, and the human who exercised the merged build closes it with a comment saying what was checked.
60	
61	The label names and this process are specific to this repository and are not used by the product's template loops, which users run against their own repositories with their own configurable trigger label and role models (tracked in [the AIDLC template loops epic on GitHub](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Atype%3Aepic%20label%3Aarea%3Atemplates)).

## Model routing

The triager sets one `impl:<model>` label and one `review:<model>` label. Use the following tiers, with xhigh reasoning:

| Tier | Model             | Use                         |
| ---- | ----------------- | --------------------------- |
| 1    | `gpt-6-luna`      | Mundane work                |
| 2    | `gpt-6.1-sol`     | Default work                |
| 3    | `claude-opus-5.5` | Harder work and sign-off    |
| 4    | `gpt-6-astra`     | Hardest work and escalation |

Whatever model family implements the change, the other family reviews it: OpenAI models are reviewed by Claude, and Claude is reviewed by an OpenAI model. If a worker cannot finish, escalate to the next tier.

## Types, areas, and milestones

Every issue has one type: `type:bug`, `type:feature`, `type:ui-polish`, `type:architecture`, `type:chore`, `type:research`, or `type:epic`. Area labels locate the affected part of the product: `area:web`, `area:editor`, `area:settings`, `area:api`, `area:engine`, `area:contracts`, `area:design-system`, `area:templates`, `area:integrations`, `area:installer`, or `area:harness`.

Milestones are `Pre-merge #151` for work that must land before the feature PR merges, `After merge: evaluate and stabilise` for product evaluation, the architecture sweep and the cutovers they require (this milestone blocks further feature work), and `Later` for queued and long-term work, with most items parked under `backlog`.

Epics carry `type:epic` and area labels only; pipelines ignore them. Each child issue starts its body with `Part of #<epic-number>`, and the epic lists its child issues.

## Development pipeline

An issue is picked up according to its gate label. The implementer named by its `impl:` label works in an isolated branch. The reviewer named by its `review:` label reviews the diff and comes from the opposite model family. A QA agent tests according to the `qa:` label and records results in the PR and the issue. `human-in-the-loop` issues additionally get human QA of the merged build, tracked as described above. `needs-plan-approval` issues get a human-approved plan before implementation. When a human QA step is required before an issue closes (by the label, or by the owner in a comment on the issue), its pull requests reference it as "Part of" rather than "Closes", the pipeline never closes it, and the human who exercised the merged build closes it with a comment saying what was checked.

The label names and this process are specific to this repository and are not used by the product's template loops, which users run against their own repositories with their own configurable trigger label and role models (tracked in [the AIDLC template loops epic on GitHub](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Atype%3Aepic%20label%3Aarea%3Atemplates)).

### Claude readiness and saved selections

Settings separates owner catalog enablement from prerequisite health. The seven server states are
`unknown`, `ready`, `cli-missing`, `cli-incompatible`, `auth`, `quota` and `transport`; `checking`
is client-only while no result exists yet.

On first load, readiness is `checking` until a result arrives; the Settings preflight card shows
"Loading preflight…". A background recheck (window focus or Retry preflight) keeps the last result
on screen. The card announces "Rechecking…" in a muted live region; when its request is paused
offline, it keeps the last result and announces "Offline; showing the last check." A completed
lookup failure or timeout replaces the card's badge list with "Could not load preflight", with no
state badge; the model picker and policy field show `unknown` instead of cached success.

After a successful lookup, **Harness preflight** shows one badge per harness with a label, never
the enum, which stays in `data-state`: Ready, Unknown, CLI not found, CLI update needed, Sign-in needed, Usage
limit, Connection failed. Missing, outdated and signed-out CLIs use the failure tone; unknown,
usage limit and connection failures the warning tone. Under it are the server's problems, each one
detail sentence and one action (for example "Claude is not signed in. Run claude auth login, then
retry preflight."). Claude rows add the adapter's model listing ("listed by adapter", neutral tone)
and state that listings do not confirm account access. **Retry preflight** in the card head
refetches and is disabled while a check runs.

**Defaults** gives each harness, Codex and Claude alike, at most one short line under its fields:
"Checking…" while the catalog first loads, the saved model's catalog problem (not in the catalog,
disabled), or "<Harness> readiness: <label>. See Harness preflight below." for a harness that is
not ready. A saved model the list does not offer stays selected as "<name> (saved)", "(disabled)"
or "(not in catalog)"; the full problem stays in Harness preflight. Catalog rows of a harness that
is not ready say "Enabled in catalog. <Harness> readiness: <label>." for Claude and Codex rows
alike; nothing is shown during the first check.

The **model picker** keeps a ready Claude field editable, with its label, through a background

1	import { defineConfig, mergeConfig } from 'vitest/config';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Shared Vitest configuration for every package and app.
5	 *
6	 * Coverage thresholds are the repository policy (docs/10-testing-and-quality.md):
7	 * at least 90% for lines, branches, functions and statements in every package. They are not tunable per
8	 * package; raise them repo-wide or add an exclusion for generated code only.
9	 *
10	 * Workspace packages declare a `development` export condition that points at their TypeScript
11	 * source. Resolving it here means tests never need another package's `dist/`: a change in a lower
12	 * package is visible to a higher package's tests without a rebuild. See ADR-0014.
13	 *
14	 * @param {import('vitest/config').UserConfig} [overrides]
15	 */
16	export function createVitestConfig(overrides = {}) {
17	  const base = defineConfig({
18	    resolve: {
19	      conditions: ['development'],
20	    },
21	    test: {
22	      include: ['src/**/*.test.ts', 'src/**/*.test.tsx'],
23	      environment: 'node',
24	      clearMocks: true,
25	      restoreMocks: true,
26	      coverage: {
27	        provider: 'v8',
28	        reporter: ['text-summary', 'json-summary', 'lcov'],
29	        reportsDirectory: './coverage',
30	        all: true,
31	        include: ['src/**/*.ts', 'src/**/*.tsx'],
32	        exclude: [
33	          'src/**/*.test.ts',
34	          'src/**/*.test.tsx',
35	          'src/**/*.d.ts',
36	          'src/**/__fixtures__/**',
37	          'src/**/generated/**',
38	        ],
39	        thresholds: {
40	          lines: 90,
41	          branches: 90,
42	          functions: 90,
43	          statements: 90,
44	        },
45	      },
46	    },
47	  });
48	  return mergeConfig(base, overrides);
49	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs each mutation of PreflightSection.tsx against the two focused test files, restoring the
# exact original bytes (sha256-checked) after every mutation and on any exit.
set -u
export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"
E="C:/Users/98jak/graphgoblin-qa/2026-11-17-five-intents/i4-442-ui-author-02/author"
WEB="G:/ggq/gg-i4-442-plugin-diagnostics/GraphGoblin/apps/web"
REL="src/settings/sections/PreflightSection.tsx"
SRC="$WEB/$REL"
BACKUP="$E/PreflightSection.tsx.original"
OUT="$E/mutations"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
cp "$SRC" "$BACKUP"
ORIGINAL="$(sha256sum "$SRC" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
restore() {
  cp "$BACKUP" "$SRC"
  local now
  now="$(sha256sum "$SRC" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  if [ "$now" != "$ORIGINAL" ]; then echo "RESTORE FAILED: $now != $ORIGINAL"; exit 99; fi
}
trap restore EXIT
node --version
echo "original sha256 $ORIGINAL"
cd "$WEB" || exit 98
for id in "$@"; do
  node "$E/mutate.mjs" "$SRC" "$id" || { restore; echo "$id: mutation not applied"; continue; }
  pnpm exec vitest run src/settings/sections/PreflightSection.test.tsx src/settings/SettingsPage.test.tsx \
    --reporter=json --outputFile="$OUT/$id.json" > "$OUT/$id.log" 2>&1
  code=$?
  restore
  node -e '
    const r = require(process.argv[1]);
    const failed = r.testResults.flatMap((f) => f.assertionResults.filter((a) => a.status === "failed").map((a) => a.fullName));
    console.log(`${process.argv[2]}: exit=${process.argv[3]} passed=${r.numPassedTests} failed=${r.numFailedTests}`);
    for (const name of failed) console.log(`    x ${name}`);
  ' "$OUT/$id.json" "$id" "$code"
done
echo "final sha256 $(sha256sum "$SRC" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

content.content:
Toggle and model-form refusals use plain sentences: **Harness models can only be enabled or disabled.** (`MODEL_MANAGED_BY_HARNESS`); **LiteLLM is not configured. Adding local models is not available yet.** (`LITELLM_NOT_CONFIGURED`); and **This model is no longer in the catalog.** (`MODEL_NOT_FOUND`). A toggle refused with 404 refreshes the catalog, announces the reason in the section, and focuses its heading if the focused row disappears. LiteLLM creation remains unavailable until the adapter ships.

On upgrade, every old row becomes `harness`, including hand-added rows. Hand-added rows keep their values but cannot be edited/deleted; disable them if unwanted. User-edited seeded names, efforts, and default efforts re-sync from the shipped catalog at startup, while enabled is preserved. GPT-6 and GPT-5.6 entries list **none (no reasoning)**, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`; **GPT-5.5** (`gpt-5.5`) lists `low` to `xhigh`, as the Codex CLI's own model catalog does. `none` is the one lowest level: Codex receives it under the name the model's family uses for that level, and the run records `none`. Every other level reaches Codex unchanged. A `none` saved for a model that does not o

In Settings **Defaults**, Claude choices are gated by readiness: when Claude is not ready, the
saved choice stays selected as "<name> (saved)" with the short help line "Claude readiness:
<label>. See Harness preflight below." Codex keeps its enabled catalog choices and shows the
same help line for Codex when it is not ready. This asymmetry is recorded for a later owner
decision in the [delivery register, section 9](../delivery/2026-10-18-i01-i07-register.md#9-pending-owner-decisions-and-acceptance).

Inspect `codex plugin list --json` and > `codex mcp list --json` in the worker directory; neither proves every enabled plugin loaded. > Verify the expected tool in the worker before relying on it. **Retry preflight**, the "Rechecking…"/"Offline" status, the loading view and the "Could not load preflight" error view are unchanged. Preflight never starts a model turn.") as `text-xs text-muted` text inside the harness row. The Codex notice is the same kind of statement, so it uses the same treatment and placement (after problems, inside the row). It is information, not status. - **Why not `Alert`.** `Alert` renders `role="status"` (a polite live region) with a tinted box and icon. A static scope note is not a status change; the card already owns exactly one live region (Rechecking…/Offline), which docs/09 and the existing test rely on; and a tinted info/ warn box under **Ready** reads as a problem with Codex, contradicting the unchanged badge. - **Why not a badge or the problems list.** A second badge beside **Ready** would look like a measured plugin state. Problems are rendered in the readiness tone and mean "fix this"; D175 explicitly declined overloading `problems`, and a Ready row has no problem list at all. - **Shown for every Codex state, after any problems.** The sentence describes the check's scope, which is the same whatever the result, exactly like the Claude note (shown in every state). Keeping it constant means the row's layout does not jump between rechecks, and the brief asks for it "alongside the unchanged readiness badge, authentication problems and Retry". The real problem always comes first in its failure/warning tone; the notice follows, muted, outside the list, so it neither hides nor competes with the error. The numbered docs/CHANGELOG describe the Settings notice in the Codex card without a readiness condition. This differs deliberately from the system report, where `plugins.codex` is a counted `warn` row and is emitted only after a passing Codex check; in Settings it is descriptive text, not a check result. No contract field, query, probe, link or plugin setting was added. Not a plugin manager. - **Accessibility.** Ordinary `

` inside the Codex `

The shared text is imported from the existing public export `CODEX_PLUGIN_OBSERVABILITY_NOTICE` of `@graphgoblin/domain`; it is not duplicated. ## What the user sees In **Settings → Harness preflight**, the Codex row reads, top to bottom: 1. unchanged readiness badge (`Ready`, `Sign-in needed`, …), `codex`, version; 2. unchanged server problems, if any, in their existing failure/warning tone list; 3. new: one muted small paragraph with the exact shared text, the two inventory commands set as inline code: > Loaded plugin tools are not verified by this check. Inspect `codex plugin list --json` and > `codex mcp list --json` in the worker directory; neither proves every enabled plugin loaded. > Verify the expected tool in the worker before relying on it. **Retry preflight**, the "Rechecking…"/"Offline" status, the loading view and the "Could not load preflight" error view are unchanged. Claude, Ollama and any other harness rows never show the notice; a result list without Codex shows none. ## Copy and layout reasoning - **Exact shared copy, no new words.** The row renders `CODEX_PLUGIN_OBSERVABILITY_NOTICE` verbatim, so Settings, `--preflight` and `GET /system/preflight` make one identical claim and the docs' quotation ("The Codex Settings card also says **Loaded plugin tools are not verified by this check.**") holds. It states the scope of *this check*; it does not say any plugin is broken, and it offers the inventory commands as investigation, with their stated limit. - **Commands as code without duplicating text.** The constant is split on a capture group (`/(codex [a-z]+ list --json)/`); odd parts render in ``, the rest as text. The DOM text is byte-for-byte the constant (tested). If the constant's wording later changes so that no command matches, it degrades to plain prose rather than breaking. Monospace makes the two commands recognisable and easy to select; `` adds no accessible-name change. - **Muted paragraph, mirroring the existing Claude scope note.** The card already states what a readiness result does *not* establish for Claude ("Adapter model listings do not confirm account access. Preflight never starts a model turn.") as `text-xs text-muted` text inside the harness row. The Codex notice is the same kind of statement, so it uses the same treatment and placement (after problems, inside the row). It is information, not status. - **Why not `Alert`.** `Alert` renders `role="status"` (a polite live region) with a tinted box and icon. A static scope note is not a status change; the card already owns exactly one live region (Rechecking…/Offline), which docs/09 and the existing test rely on; and a tinted info/ warn box under **Ready** reads as a problem with Codex, contradicting the unchanged badge. - **Why not a badge or the problems list.** A second badge beside **Ready** would look like a measured plugin state. Problems are rendered in the readiness tone and mean "fix this"; D175 explicitly declined overloading `problems`, and a Ready row has no problem list at all. - **Shown for every Codex state, after any problems.** The sentence describes the check's scope, which is the same whatever the result, exactly like the Claude note (shown in every state). Keeping it constant means the row's layout does not jump between rechecks, and the brief asks for it "alongside the unchanged readiness badge, authentication problems and Retry". The real problem always comes first in its failure/warning tone; the notice follows, muted, outside the list, so it neither hides nor competes with the error. The numbered docs/CHANGELOG describe the Settings notice in the Codex card without a readiness condition. This differs deliberately from the system report, where `plugins.codex` is a counted `warn` row and is emitted only after a passing Codex check; in Settings it is descriptive text, not a check result. The Codex notice is in place in Settings → Harness preflight, and it's ready for the GPT UI review. All changes are uncommitted and nothing is staged. HEAD is still `5b0d806c`, and the seven frozen backend and docs files still match the root receipt.

**Files changed (my three only)**
- `apps/web/src/settings/sections/PreflightSection.tsx` (+24 lines)
- `apps/web/src/settings/sections/PreflightSection.test.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/settings/SettingsPage.test.tsx`

**What the user sees**
- The Codex row has a small muted paragraph containing the shared constant word for word. It's imported from `@graphgoblin/domain`, not copied.
- The two inventory commands are shown as code by splitting the constant itself, so the visible text is exactly the shared text.
- It sits after any problems and outside the problem list. The badge, problems, Retry, Rechecking/Offline status, loading view and error view are unchanged.
- No new query, request, contract field or control.
- Claude, Ollama and other rows never show it, and neither does a result list without Codex.

**Design choices**
- **Muted paragraph, not `Alert`:** this copies the existing Claude note ("Adapter model listings do not confirm account access"). `Alert` would add a second live region in a card whose tests rely on exactly one. A tinted box under Ready would also read as a problem with Codex.
- **Not a badge, not the problems list:** a second badge would look like a measured plugin state, and D175 ruled out using `problems`.
- **Shown for every Codex state, not only Ready:** it describes what the check covers, which is the same whatever the result. The brief asks for it alongside the sign-in problems, and the docs don't limit it to Ready. This is the one deliberate difference from the backend, which adds its warning only when Codex passes. If the reviewer prefers Ready-only, it's a one-condition change.

**Checks (all retained in `i4-442-ui-author-02/author/`)**
- **Before edits:** the two focused test files passed, 48 tests.
- **Final:** 59 tests pass (11 new). The web typecheck, ESLint with zero warnings and Prettier all pass.
- **Focused coverage on `PreflightSection.tsx`:** passes the unchanged 90% thresholds (100% statements, functions and lines; 96.42% branches). The one uncovered branch is older Claude code (`84d641a`).
- **Mutation testing:** I made nine deliberately wrong versions of the component, and the tests failed for all nine. They covered: notice removed, on every harness, Ready-only, warning colour, live region, no code formatting, visually hidden, placed before the problems, and wording changed. The file was restored and hash-checked after each one. Afterwards only a comment changed.
- **Failures:** no gate check failed. One read-only diff command failed on a shell quirk and was redone with `diff -u`; the report records it.

**Still open**
- **`docs/09-frontend-and-pwa.md` (lines 1064–1071) doesn't mention the Codex notice.** That's the docs owner's file, so I didn't edit it; suggested wording is in the report.
- **Not checked in a real browser:** the unit tests don't load CSS, so real rendering, wrapping at narrow widths and screen-reader order still need browser QA. Two browser test files touch this card: `responsive.spec.ts` (sideways scroll) and `readiness.spec.ts` (single status region). Per the brief, I didn't run them.
- These are author tests only. GPT review, browser QA, CI and the final audit remain separate gates, and #439, #442 and owner acceptance stay open.

The full report, with copy and layout reasoning, is `REPORT.md` in `i4-442-ui-author-02/author/`, and the final patch is `10-final-uncommitted.patch`.
